summary: Okeechobee County Airport (OBE/KOBE) is a small, county-owned public-use airport serving the rural community of Okeechobee, Florida, located inland near the northern shore of Lake Okeechobee, the largest freshwater lake in the state. The facility primarily supports general aviation, flight training, recreational flying, and agricultural aircraft operations common to the surrounding ranch and cattle country. Its modest infrastructure and scenic central-Florida setting make it a convenient gateway for visitors heading to Lake Okeechobee fishing, hunting, and eco-tourism destinations.
faqs:
Q: What type of airport is Okeechobee County Airport?
A: It is a small, publicly owned general aviation airport operated by Okeechobee County, with no scheduled commercial airline service.

Q: Are there any restaurants or amenities on site?
A: The airport has limited amenities typical of small general aviation fields. Pilots and visitors typically find food, fuel, and supplies in nearby Okeechobee, just a short drive from the airfield.

Q: Can I rent a car at the airport?
A: Rental cars are not available on-site. Visitors should arrange rentals in advance through agencies located in Okeechobee or larger nearby cities such as Sebring or Fort Pierce.

Q: What is the airport commonly used for?
A: It serves recreational flying, flight training, agricultural aviation, and private aircraft visiting the Lake Okeechobee region for fishing and outdoor recreation.
transport_tips: The airport is located just a few miles southeast of downtown Okeechobee, easily reached by a short drive along US-98/SR-700. Taxi and rideshare options are limited in this rural area, so renting a car or arranging pickup with a local hotel is recommended. Visitors flying in privately will find tie-downs and transient parking available at the FBO.
local_tip: If you are visiting for bass fishing on Lake Okeechobee, ask local pilots about the small seaplane-friendly ramps and bait shops near the lake's north shore—many GA pilots fly directly to waterfront lodges instead of using the county airport.
